findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the guard's 'stale id' test follow the existing constants (config.DEFAULT_MODEL, config.VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL, model_classes.TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL) rather than a hand-written pre-5.5 regex, or state explicitly that the regex cutoff must be bumped with each model-generation epic.
evidence: Plan step 1: 'whose string matches a pre-5.5 Claude id (`claude-(opus|sonnet|haiku)-[1-4]...`, `claude-[1-3]-...`)'

Existing sources of truth: src/rebar/llm/config.py:61 `DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-opus-5-5"`, config.py:67 `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5-5"`, model_classes.py:45 `TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-haiku-5-5"`; model_classes.py:53-56 `_DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS` maps class names to these three
Problem statement: the defect is a hard-coded id that did not follow the epic's model move
findings.finding: The new guard hard-codes the generation cutoff in its regex (`claude-(opus|sonnet|haiku)-[1-4]...`, `claude-[1-3]-...`). The list of current model ids already lives in `config.DEFAULT_MODEL`, `config.VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL` and `model_classes.TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL`, so the guard repeats that knowledge by hand. The guard therefore freezes the boundary at 5.5. After the next model move, a leftover `"claude-sonnet-5-5"` literal default would pass it, which is the same 'frozen id goes stale' defect this plan fixes. Each future bump would need someone to edit the regex by hand.
scenarios: The next epic moves the configured models to a 6.x generation. A new or leftover module-level `X = "claude-sonnet-5-5"` or a `model="claude-opus-5-5"` default in src/rebar is not matched by the `[1-4]` pattern, so the guard passes while the default is stale.
findings.suggested_fix: In the test, build `CURRENT = {config.DEFAULT_MODEL, config.VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL, model_classes.TRIVIAL_DEFAULT_MODEL}`. Flag any function default or module-level string constant that names a Claude id (regex `claude-(opus|sonnet|haiku)-\d`) unless it is, or contains, a member of CURRENT. Containment matters for qualified ids such as bedrock_model.py:22 `"us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5-5"`. Alternatively, keep the regex and add a comment plus an AC line saying the cutoff is bumped together with the config constants.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reword step 3's rationale: `_MODEL` follows the code-level standard-class default constant (on purpose, not operator config), so emitted specs stay deterministic.
evidence: Plan step 3: 'so it follows the configured standard-class default instead of a frozen id'
src/rebar/llm/config.py:67: `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5-5"` (code constant)
src/rebar/llm/model_classes.py:206: per-class resolution `raw.get("model") or _DEFAULT_MODEL_BY_CLASS[name]` is where operator configuration takes effect
tests/unit/test_fixture_emit.py docstring: 'emit byte-identical trees on repeat runs'
findings.finding: Step 3 says deriving `_MODEL` from `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL` makes it 'follow the configured standard-class default'. That is not what the mechanism does. `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL` is a code constant read at import time; an operator's `REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL` or `[tool.rebar.llm]` standard-class model never reaches it. Resolution through model_classes would honor configuration, but it would make emitted specs depend on the environment and break the byte-identical repeat-emit guarantee. An implementer who takes the word 'configured' literally might reach for that resolution.
scenarios: The implementer resolves the standard class at emit time to match 'configured'. Emitted specs then differ between machines with different REBAR_LLM_STANDARD_MODEL settings.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'so it follows the configured standard-class default instead of a frozen id' with 'so it tracks the code-level standard-class default constant (deliberately not operator/env configuration, keeping emitted specs deterministic) instead of a separately frozen id'.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] In step 3, decide which model `fixture_admission._pass1_model` should fall back to (frontier `DEFAULT_MODEL`, which matches `PASS_MODEL_CLASS["pass1"]`, or the standard-class `_MODEL`) and state that choice in the plan.
evidence: Plan step 3: "Set it to `f\"anthropic:{VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL}\"` ... so it follows the configured standard-class default ... and as the fallback in `fixture_admission._pass1_model`."
src/rebar/llm/evals/fixture_admission.py:423-428: `_pass1_model` returns the first usage row's `model`, else `fixture_emit._MODEL`.
src/rebar/llm/evals/plan_replay/parity.py:23: `PASS_MODEL_CLASS = {"pass1": "frontier", "pass2": "standard"}`.
src/rebar/llm/config.py:61,67: `DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-opus-5-5"` (frontier) vs `VERIFIER_DEFAULT_MODEL = "claude-sonnet-5-5"` (verifier/standard).
findings.finding: Step 3 sets `fixture_emit._MODEL` to the standard-class default (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) and acknowledges it is also the fallback in `fixture_admission._pass1_model`. That fallback names the model PASS 1 ran on, but the repo maps pass1 to the frontier class, and production pass1 defaults to `DEFAULT_MODEL = claude-opus-5-5`. So when usage rows carry no `model`, the fallback credits pass1 to the standard class instead of the frontier model that actually ran it. The plan does not say whether this standard-class fallback for pass1 is intended.
scenarios: A fixture-admission run whose usage rows have no `model` field records pass1 as `anthropic:claude-sonnet-5-5`, while the pass1 review actually ran on `claude-opus-5-5`, so the replay/parity data is credited to the wrong model class.
